title: WiFi / Wireless Assessment Surface Foundation
goal: Add WiFi as a first-class AegisPT assessment surface with passive-first wireless discovery, explicit site/SSID/BSSID authorization, adapter readiness checks, AP security posture review, rogue/unknown AP detection against an allowlist, and clearly gated intrusive wireless options.
scope: Design and implement the first safe WiFi assessment lane. Add a wizard tile for WiFi / Wireless Assessment, Settings readiness for wireless adapters and monitor-mode capability, a passive WLAN survey runner, inventory/evidence import for SSID/BSSID/channel/security/vendor/signal metadata, findings for weak or unexpected wireless posture, Mission Control/Live Agents visibility for wireless tasks, and report sections for WiFi posture. Intrusive wireless actions such as deauthentication, handshake capture, WPS PIN testing, evil-twin simulation, or jamming-style behavior must stay unavailable unless a later explicitly approved intrusive task adds the required gates.
generation_reason: The operator identified WiFi analysis as a missing pentest-suite capability. The repo search found no existing first-class WiFi assessment lane beyond incidental wireless-AP device labels in IoT default credentials.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: WiFi foundation only. Keep the first slice passive-first and evidence-first. Do not add deauthentication, jamming, evil-twin simulation, WPS PIN brute force, credential harvesting, or live RF disruption without a separate future intrusive task and explicit authorization gates.

success_criteria: Wizard exposes a WiFi / Wireless Assessment tile that requires site/location, approved SSIDs, approved BSSIDs where known, exclusions, and wireless adapter/interface context before launch.
Settings exposes wireless readiness: detected adapters, monitor-mode capability, required binaries, channel support, safe parallelism limits, and clear blocked/degraded states.

Passive WLAN survey runner records SSID, BSSID, channel, band, encryption/auth mode, PMF/WPA2/WPA3/WEP/open/WPS hints, vendor/OUI where available, signal strength, and observation timestamp without disrupting the network.
Inventory stores wireless access points and networks using existing provenance/evidence patterns without changing protected finding schema fields.

Findings are evidence-backed and conservative: open networks, WEP/TKIP, WPS enabled, missing PMF where relevant, rogue/unknown AP against allowlist, duplicate/evil-twin-like SSID/BSSID anomalies, and weak guest-network posture where observable.
Mission Control and Live Agents show what wireless task is doing, which adapter/channel/SSID is in focus, and what evidence has been captured.
Reports include a WiFi Security Summary section only when WiFi evidence exists, with explicit coverage, limitations, and legal boundary notes.
No intrusive wireless behavior is available or implied in the foundation slice unless a future task adds explicit gates and validation.
out_of_scope: Handshake capture or password cracking without a separate intrusive authorization task
Automatically enabling monitor mode on a live adapter during an active assessment without operator confirmation
Claiming WiFi support without adapter/lab validation evidence

required_checks: Focused runner unit tests with fixture iw/airodump-style outputs and no RF hardware dependency
API tests proving WiFi profile creation, scope/ROE validation, and inventory import
Browser tests for the WiFi wizard tile, Settings readiness states, Mission Control task visibility, and WiFi report section
Safe host-readiness validation showing supported, degraded, and missing-adapter states without launching RF-disruptive actions
acceptance_criteria: A WiFi assessment can be prepared and launched only after explicit wireless ROE is acknowledged.
A fixture-backed passive survey produces inventory, findings, Mission Control visibility, and report output.
Intrusive wireless actions remain blocked/unavailable in this foundation slice.
A readiness artifact under codex/results/ documents adapter/tool state and remaining lab-validation gaps.

before_promotion: Earlier queued stabilization and product-truth tasks have completed or the operator explicitly promotes this wireless capability earlier.
NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the only active task.
after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.
